title: Bug: "Error: Invalid interface name(s): ..." in fdb/test_fdb_mac_learning.py
author: wrideout-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

In some cases, fdb testing may be run on a DUT which does not have fully sequential interfaces.  Given such a DUT which has Ethernet4, 8, and 12 configured, but no others, we may attempt to run the following CLI command:

```
sudo config interface startup Ethernet4-12
```

Doing so is an invalid command due to missing interfaces, and so the following error is returned:
```
Error: Invalid interface name(s): Ethernet5, Ethernet6, Ethernet7, Ethernet9, Ethernet10, Ethernet11
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Run fdb.test_fdb_mac_learning.TestFdbMacLearning on a test topology including a DUT with non-sequential interface naming.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Test should not assume the full range of interfaces is available.

### Relevant log output

```shell
"tests.common.errors.RunAnsibleModuleFail: run module shell failed, Ansible Results =>\nfailed = True\nchanged = True\nrc = 2\ncmd = sudo config interface startup Ethernet4-12\nstart = 2026-04-07 21:43:22.878682\nend = 2026-04-07 21:43:23.774331\ndelta = 0:00:00.895649\nmsg = non-zero return code\ninvocation = {'module_args': {'_raw_params': 'sudo config interface startup Ethernet4-12', '_uses_shell': True, 'expand_argument_vars': True, 'stdin_add_newline': True, 'strip_empty_ends': True, 'argv': None, 'chdir': None, 'executable': None, 'creates': None, 'removes': None, 'stdin': None}}\n_ansible_no_log = False\nstdout =\nstderr =\nUsage: config interface startup [OPTIONS] <interface_name>\nTry 'config interface startup -h' for help.\n\nError: Invalid interface name(s): Ethernet5, Ethernet6, Ethernet7, Ethernet9, Ethernet10, Ethernet11"
```

### Output of `show version`

```shell

```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

linkedPullRequests.title: Fix intf startup in fdb tests
linkedPullRequests.author: wrideout-arista
linkedPullRequests.body:
Target ports for startup command may not be fully sequential (gaps may exist), which causes CLI syntax issues in the test.

Don't assume no gaps in the sequence, and use a more explicit CLI command.
